Hi Sofia,

Quick one from our Legal team: before we sign the PO we need concrete artifacts that show how data residency and customer-controlled storage are enforced in the Private (VPC) deployment you proposed. Specifically:

- How do you prove tenant data never leaves our region (control-plane vs data-plane split)?
- If we ask for a tenant wipe, what evidence do you provide and what is the typical timeline?
- How are backups/snapshots handled across AZs and what is your retention policy?

Can you share a short list of artifacts (certs, runbooks, logs) and an example timeline for an erase request? We also need to know whether any third-party backups (cloud snapshots) are stored outside our region.

Hi Jacob — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marcus (Security & Compliance) and Marissa (Solutions) to provide artifacts and the erase runbook.

High level answers up front:
- Data plane stays in-customer-region for Private/VPC: compute and storage are provisioned into your VPC subnets; control plane communications can be configured over customer-managed endpoints.
- Erase: we provide a signed evidence package including deletion runbook, snapshot deletion logs, and a verification checklist. Typical end-to-end timeline for a standard tenant wipe is 3–7 business days (depends on snapshot deletion windows and any legal holds).
- Backups: snapshots are stored in your cloud account when using customer-managed storage. For Redwood-managed backups (rare, opt-in), snapshots are restricted to specified regions; we can commit region-locked storage in the contract.

We have a starter evidence bundle linked below; Marcus will confirm what we can share today and what requires an NDA/contract clause.

Thanks — adding technical detail and the artifacts we can attach immediately. I'm pasting an abbreviated Q&A and attaching the evidence matrix. Full attachments: residency_evidence_matrix.xlsx, residency_cert.pdf, snap-delete-runbook.txt

-- Q: How do you prove tenant data never leaves our region?
A: For Private/VPC deployments we deploy inference nodes and storage volumes (EBS/managed NFS) into customer subnets. Network egress is controlled by customer VPC NAT/GW and security groups. We provide:
  * Architecture diagram showing control-plane vs data-plane endpoints, IP ranges, and peering configuration.
  * Network flow logs (sample) and a signed statement that no automated cross-region replication is enabled.
  * Residency certificate (residency_cert.pdf) that enumerates the policy binding for your account.

-- Q: Snapshots & backups across AZs?
A: Snapshots by design are AZ-attached; however cloud provider snapshot stores may replicate metadata regionally but not cross-region unless explicitly configured. We document:
  * Default snapshot lifecycle (retention 30d, configurable).
  * Snapshot deletion runbook with verifiable steps and generated job IDs (snap-delete-runbook.txt).
  * If you opt for customer-managed snapshots (recommended), all snapshot artifacts live in your cloud account and we do not copy them.

-- Q: Erase request evidence and timeline?
A: Evidence package includes deletion job IDs, block device wipe start/complete timestamps, snapshot deletion logs, KV cache invalidation record, and a signed attestation. Typical timeline:
  * Day 0: Request received and triage (same day).
  * Day 1–2: Snapshot deletion jobs initiated and confirmation logs collected.
  * Day 3–5: Final device sanitize operations and attestation prepared.
  * Day 6–7: Delivery of signed evidence package (accelerated workflow available for an SLA).

-- Q: Third-party backups?
A: We only use third-party backup storage if explicitly enabled in contract. By default there are no external vendor backups for Private deployments. If required, we will include a clause enforcing same-region storage and audited controls.

Notes: For any items that require an NDA (full sample logs containing internal IPs) we will provide redacted samples first.

Marcus Lin
Head, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Marcus — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from Legal/Infrastructure:

2) We have an internal retention hold process (legal hold) that could prevent deletion for up to 60 days. How does that interact with your wipe SLA?

Also — can you confirm whether any logs or artifacts in the evidence package include PII in clear text; if so we need to understand redaction options.

Jacob

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Residency proof & wipe scenarios for private deployment

Jacob — quick answers and next steps (ETA for docs and sample evidence below).

1) Snapshot deletion failures: our orchestrator surfaces job status and failure codes to your admin console (job ID + human-readable cause). By default we perform 3 automated retries spaced by exponential backoff; failed jobs are then escalated to on-call infra with an incident ticket (SEC-459). We will provide the job ID and full retry log as part of the evidence bundle.

2) Legal holds: if Novamed asserts a legal hold we will pause the wipe workflow and surface the hold metadata in the evidence package (hold issuer, timestamp). The wipe SLA is paused for the duration of a legitimate legal hold; we can include a contractual clause to require Novamed to lift holds within a defined escalation window or to accept adjusted timelines.

3) PII in logs: default evidence artifacts are redacted for PII. If Novamed requests unredacted logs for e-discovery, that requires a scoped legal process and an additional access control workflow (we'll note this in the contract).

Next steps and deliverables:
- Today: share redacted residency evidence matrix and residency_cert.pdf (attached).
- EOD tomorrow: sample deletion job logs (redacted) and the snap-delete-runbook draft.
- If helpful, schedule a 30-minute runbook review with your infra team — propose Fri 15 May 10:00 PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
